outcome: Define durable ContextResolution identity, provenance, currentness and materialization semantics so Oracle results can be cached, replayed and recovered safely while preserving existing manifest-protected artifact guarantees.
currentProblem: Runtime resolutions may span multiple providers, staged retrieval and cached materializations. Without first-class identity/currentness, a changed repository head, artifact, index or graph can silently reuse stale context; crash recovery can also replay an incompatible resolution even if individual source reads remain correct.
constraints: Resolution identity binds the requirement plus source/currentness inputs and the relevant planner/provider configuration.
Derived or graph context retains traceable source provenance rather than replacing source identity with an opaque summary.
Existing manifest-protected QA artifact reads remain fail-closed on producer, revision, acceptance and content mismatch.
Recovery may reuse a resolution only when its currentness fences still match; ambiguous external outcomes cannot be treated as current.
Invalidation is explicit and selective; cache reuse is an optimization and never acceptance authority.
Persistence technology is selected only after identity/update/recovery experiments establish the required semantics.
successCriteria: The same requirement against the same authoritative source/currentness state has deterministic reuse identity; relevant source change invalidates it.
Every materialized context item can be traced to source provenance and currentness evidence, including graph-derived context.
Crash/replay and concurrent refresh cannot promote a stale ContextResolution to current.
Manifest-protected Backend-to-QA continuation remains at least as strict as the existing behavior.
Failure-injection tests cover stale source, partial provider failure, interrupted materialization and recovery.
